title: CursorHide causes cursor to permanently disappear on login screen

judgment.rationale: The latest comment reports the cursor disappearing on the lock screen after keyboard input and occasional hiding in Firefox. The secure-desktop transition is a plausible trigger, but the current issue has no controlled repro or confirmed visibility-state mechanism.
evidence: The original reporter says the cursor disappears on the lock screen after enabling CursorHide.
A later commenter reports the cursor disappears after typing on the lock screen and has rarely seen it hidden in Firefox.
The latest comment provides lock-screen input and intermittent Firefox scenarios, but no steps that establish the trigger.

The cursor hider's visibility operations are the relevant state boundary. Source at pinned main (237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c): https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/mouseutils/AutoHideCursor/SystemCursorHider.h
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the issue-specific scenario: Restore cursor visibility when the active desktop changes

fix_assessment.rationale: The possible hook/cursor visibility path needs a maintainer reproduction before choosing a safe restore behavior.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore cursor visibility when the active desktop changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: CursorHide may retain a hidden cursor state when input moves to the lock/secure desktop or a different foreground context, and the normal restoration callback is missed.
plan: Reproduce the lock-screen and Firefox cases with CursorHide enabled and identify whether the active input desktop changes before cursor visibility is lost.
If the hide state survives the desktop transition, restore cursor visibility when the utility deactivates or loses its supported desktop context.
Add a regression for lock/unlock and context switching that verifies cursor visibility is restored.
verification: Typing on the lock screen never leaves the cursor hidden after returning to the desktop.
Hiding over Firefox does not persist after the configured inactivity/utility conditions end.

actions.label: Restore cursor visibility when the active desktop changes

reproduce.title: Restore cursor visibility when the active desktop changes
prerequisites: CursorHide enabled with its configured hide condition.
A test account that can reach the Windows lock screen.
steps: Enable CursorHide and confirm the cursor is visible on the desktop.
Lock Windows and type a character at the sign-in screen.
Unlock and check whether the cursor is visible without moving the mouse.
Separately reproduce the reported Firefox case and note whether the configured hide timeout is active.
reproduce.expected_result: The cursor is visible on the sign-in/desktop contexts and is restored when CursorHide no longer owns the active context.

comment.body: Thanks for the lock-screen and Firefox observations. After the cursor becomes hidden on the lock screen and you unlock, could you note whether moving the mouse, waiting for the configured timeout, or restarting CursorHide restores it? Please report which action first restores visibility; this will help distinguish a retained hide state from a missed restore on context change.
